title: Whoever Is Hungry
logline: Every evening, one person feeds the same stray dogs by name and checks their wounds. Every evening, passers-by toss them scraps to watch them scramble.
human_question: Can the same act of giving be, at the same time, a kindness and a private pleasure?

premise.story: An evening routine of feeding stray dogs at a public gathering place: the regular feeder's bowls, names and care, and the different, lighter gestures of passers-by, children and visitors who feed the same dogs for the fun of watching them eat.
premise.place: A bus stand, temple compound or market square where stray dogs gather each evening.
premise.experience: The quiet discipline of one person's routine against the passing amusement of a crowd; the dogs themselves, indifferent to anyone's reasons.

concept_links.why: This is close to the concept's own example: feeding an animal to enjoy watching it eat is one of the occasions greed-rooted minds arise, while feeding it out of care is counted differently, without judging either person on screen [C005-M:L21].

The regular feeder's steady, unprompted routine, sustained without anyone urging them, echoes the concept's account of effort and desire-to-act that need no push from outside [C021-M:L19] [C021-P:L53].

what_camera_could_observe: Bowls set out, dogs recognised by name
Children or visitors tossing scraps to watch a scramble
The dogs themselves, at rest and at the moment food appears
The feeder's routine ending as the light goes
what_must_be_real: The feeder's actual routine and the passers-by's own, unstaged behaviour. No one is prompted to feed the dogs for the camera.

possible_arc.opening: Dusk; dogs gathering as if they know the hour.
possible_arc.turn: A crowd of passers-by feeds the dogs for the spectacle of it.
possible_arc.ending_open: The feeder finishes their round, or doesn't, as it actually happens.

requirements: A public place with a consistent stray-dog population and a known regular feeder
Consent from the feeder to be followed over several evenings
Passers-by willing to be filmed in an ordinary public space

suggestions.name: A bus stand or temple compound in Kandy town
suggestions.why: A well-known town centre with public gathering places where stray animals are commonly present.
suggestions.verify: No feeder has been identified or contacted; this is a plausible setting only.

risks: Sentimentality about strays and their feeders
Animal welfare concerns must not be turned into a lecture
drop_if: No consistent, willing feeder can be found and followed

connections.note: Both are about giving something to eat, and whose pleasure the giving is really for.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
